title: Bent Pine Patrol

summary.short: Bin and Peri test the Bent Pine line before Haven can settle.
summary.default: Two months of nightmare prep and one hour of warm welcome. Then Peri drags Bin straight back into the trees because the patrol board is the wrong color and the wrong number, and someone has to walk Bent Pine before the next civilian patrol does it on faith.

completionOps.title: Story Sync: Bent Pine Patrol
completionOps.summary: The Bent Pine route stays unstable after a live patrol check.

nodes.text: The gate office still smells like wet wool and brick coffee. Captain Lysa has spread her notes across three columns: rumor, witness, paperwork. Bin's name appears in every column. Twice in two of them. The map of Bent Pine is laid out on the table like an autopsy nobody has the stomach to start.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Glad you walked in alive. I have three pins missing from this board and two patrols who came back chewed. The civilians want answers. The smart ones know I do not have any yet. Walk Bent Pine with me, and walk it loud — I want to know what flinches first when it hears us coming.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: The system has annotated three of the missing pins with the word ROAMING in helpful red. The fourth pin is missing because the captain knocked it off her desk yesterday and chose not to find it. I admire the discipline.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Define structured. Define small. Also define suffering, because the last three uses of those words ended with me bleeding on someone else's roof. I have not slept on a real bed in two months, Captain. Promise me bad jokes on the way home and I will walk this for you.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Bad jokes guaranteed. Cover the ridge markers, sweep south through Bent Pine, return by sundown or earlier. If something rushes you face-first, do not be brave — be loud. I want signal flares, not silent heroics. The pins on this board are already too dramatic.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Translation: walk the route, react to traps, push to Watch Ridge. Objective reveals at sixty percent explored. The system has reserved a back-row seat with popcorn and a clipboard.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Then we choose the opening. We can hug the ridge markers and play disciplined — slower, cleaner, easier to call for help. Or we can cut through Bent Pine early and try to surprise whatever has been treating this line like a buffet.

choices.label: Hold to the ridge markers
choices.summary: Disciplined approach. Visible, audible, lower danger but slower.

ops.text: Story route: the patrol stays disciplined and visible.

choices.label: Cut through Bent Pine early
choices.summary: Faster and louder. +1 danger, but you might force the contact onto your terms.

ops.text: Story route: Bin pushes the patrol into the trees for speed.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: If the route is alive, we walk it before it learns our names. Cover the shoulders, watch the snowpack, do not look surprised when the trees do something rude. Peri — if I duck, you duck. If you duck, I am already on the ground.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Acknowledged. The system is logging the duck protocol. It rates your shoulder check a friendly nine. Move.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: That sounded reckless enough to count as confidence. Move. The system has reserved a back row seat in case you embarrass yourself, and also a small bandage budget.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Bandage budget. Cool. New favorite phrase. Walking now, regretting later.
Patrol Bent Pine, react to traps and roaming contact, and push through to Watch Ridge. The grid map runs with moving monsters; objective reveals at sixty percent explored.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Watch Ridge is still standing, which is more than I promised. The thing crossing the line did not catch us, but it caught the bark off two pines and somebody's hat. Now we tell the gate this line stays dangerous until someone clears it properly. That paperwork has your name on it whether you like it or not.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Good. I will write it cleanly. Bent Pine stays closed unless escorted. Whatever that was, it hunts on a loop — patient about the wrong things, fast about the right ones. We do not solve that with one patrol.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: We got pushed off the line. Next pass needs fresh supplies, less pride, and maybe fewer things that sprint straight into your face. Frostbitten is going to enjoy the report exactly zero amount. So will I.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Listed in the ledger as: tactical retreat, no fatalities, hat lost. We will dress it up at the gate. The town does not need heroics — it needs a working sentence about the threat. We can give them that.
The patrol breaks off before the ridge call is settled. Frostbitten will have questions waiting and the answers will be the wrong shape. The kind of shape a small town fills in for you, badly.

nodes.summary: Patrol report queued for the gate; Bent Pine confirmed unstable.

ops.text: Bent Pine patrol filed. Next chapter: report at the gate.
